profile.reading:
This facility sits on Oak Road on Stanford University's campus in Stanford, California, in the northwest portion of the university's landholdings in Santa Clara County. Stanford is one of the largest private research universities in the country, and like any institution of its size and research intensity, it operates its own campus network and computing infrastructure rather than relying solely on outside providers, supporting everything from student and administrative systems to the immense data demands of Stanford's science and engineering research.

A building named for its role as both a data center and a communications hub fits naturally into how a large research university organizes its network. Universities of Stanford's scale typically maintain one or more core facilities where campus fiber, internet peering connections, and central computing equipment physically converge, functioning as the backbone through which the rest of the university's network traffic passes. Placing such a facility on the northwest edge of central campus, along Oak Road, is consistent with how large campuses site critical infrastructure away from the dense academic core while keeping it within reach of the fiber routes that connect academic buildings, laboratories, dormitories, and administrative offices.

Stanford's own public communications, including its central university website and its University IT organization's published materials, describe the university's history, academic programs, and technology strategy in broad terms, but do not name this particular building, give its square footage, or publish an IT load figure for it. That is a common pattern for university operated infrastructure: unlike a commercial colocation provider marketing capacity to tenants, a university's internal data center exists to serve the institution itself, and there is little commercial incentive to publish the kind of specification sheet a colocation operator would.

What can be documented is the location and the plausible role the building plays. Oak Road sits within Stanford's core campus footprint in an unincorporated area of Santa Clara County, a setting consistent with permanent university infrastructure rather than a temporary or leased facility. Beyond that location and the reasonable inference drawn from the building's name and Stanford's scale as a research institution, the specific technical characteristics of this data center and communications hub are not part of any public record located during this research.
